The charcoal piece is the same shape as the yellow target (char == yellow, both 9x9 "7" mirrored). The yellow target is at rows 45-53, columns 51-59.
Maybe the goal is: move the charcoal piece onto the yellow target (overlap) to complete the level. The black piece is a "shadow" partner that moves symmetrically — a constraint that makes the puzzle interesting: the pair moves as a unit (translation only, mirror-symmetric).
Wait, but the pair moves as a unit: both translate together. So the relative position between black and charcoal is fixed. To place charcoal on top of yellow: charcoal is currently at rows 12-20, columns 36-44; yellow is at rows 45-53, columns 51-59. Charcoal needs to move +33 rows, +15 columns. But the pair moves symmetrically: if charcoal moves down 33, black also moves down 33 (black rows 12-20 → 45-53, columns 18-26). And if charcoal moves right 15, black moves left 15 (columns 18-26 → 3-11). That's fine — black just ends up at rows 45-53, columns 3-11. No collision.
But wait — is the movement really symmetric, or does each arrow move both pieces in the same direction? RIGHT moved black +3 columns and charcoal -3 columns. So it's symmetric (mirror) movement. UP moved both -3 rows. So vertical moves are the same for both, horizontal moves are mirrored.
Therefore, to align charcoal with yellow: charcoal needs Δrow=+33, Δcol=+15. Each DOWN gives +3 rows; each RIGHT gives charcoal -3 columns (wrong direction). LEFT gives charcoal +3 columns. So we need 11 DOWNs and 5 LEFTs.
After that: charcoal at rows 45-53, columns 51-59 = exactly on top of yellow. Black at rows 45-53, columns 18-26-15=3-11.
But wait — does the level complete when charcoal overlaps yellow? Or does the black piece need to do something? The black piece has white dots — maybe black is the "player" and the goal is to bring the black piece to... hmm, but the black piece is a mirror image of yellow, so it can't overlap exactly.
Alternatively, the goal might be to make the two pieces (black + charcoal) form a complete shape when they meet at the center. When they overlap at the center: black at columns 27-35, charcoal at columns 27-35, same rows → the union forms a 3x9 top bar + left leg (charcoal's leg at columns 27-29) + right leg (black's leg at columns 33-35) = a "∏" shape (3x9 top bar + 6x3 legs on both ends). That's a "gate" shape. Maybe that's the goal: form a gate/arch?
Hmm. Which is it? The yellow target at the bottom right is exactly the same shape as the charcoal piece. That strongly suggests "move the charcoal piece onto the yellow target." But why is there a black piece with dots? Maybe the black piece is the actual player, and the charcoal is... hmm.

The goal might be: bring the black piece to a position where it... The black piece is a mirror image of the charcoal piece. If the black piece moves to the right half and overlaps with the charcoal piece, the mirror images combine into a "∏".
Let me think about the dots: the dots are at relative positions (1,1),(1,4),(1,7),(4,7),(7,7) — a small "7" pattern (3 dots across the top, 2 dots down the right side). Actually, the top bar of the black piece is 3 rows; the dots are only in the middle row of the bar. The dots trace the shape of the piece itself (a "7" made of dots). So the dots are just decoration indicating the piece's shape.
Another thought: this might be a "Tangram/shape-fit" game where you need to place the black piece into the outline of the yellow target. But the shapes are mirror images... unless you can flip with SPACE/ACTION7. Let me test SPACE and ACTION7 to see what they do.
